status: G4 pilot: processed, compressed and reviewed; ships as g4-ox, in Chapters VIII and X (the desktop app only)
use: Two draught oxen, unyoked, resting beside the ox cart in the quartermaster's court beyond the board (Chapters VIII and X): one model set out twice.

generator.prompt: A Roman draught ox of the mid-3rd century AD standing square: all four legs straight and vertical, evenly spaced, head held level and facing forward, tail hanging straight down, symmetrical. A heavy, deep-chested working ox about 1.45 metres at the withers with a pale dun-grey coat shading to darker grey on the neck and shoulders, a loose dewlap, medium-length upward-curving horns with dark tips, a dark muzzle and a plain hemp rope halter. No yoke, no harness, no cart, no plough, no rider, no people. Realistic proportions, anatomically accurate. Single isolated model with complete geometry from every side and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above. No ground plane, no display plinth, no text or inscriptions, no modern objects, no fantasy elements.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the camps in the desktop build at High
review.notes: A heavy pale grey ox with long upward-curving horns, a dewlap and a rope halter, as asked: 2.25 m long and 1.6 m to its horn tips. In Chapter VIII's camp the pair stand unyoked beside the ox cart, on its far side from the board, and read as oxen at once, even in the camp's rain.
